::: proof
A Poisson distribution's mean and variance both equal its mean parameter,
so $\E{Y \mid \Lambda} = \Lambda$ and $\Var{Y \mid \Lambda} = \Lambda$.
By the [law of total expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-lie):

$$
\ba
\E{Y}
&= \E{\E{Y \mid \Lambda}}
&& \text{(law of total expectation)} \\
&= \E{\Lambda}
&& \text{(Poisson mean)} \\
&= \mu
&& \text{(mean of } \Lambda \text{)}
\ea
$$

By the [law of total variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-total-variance):

$$
\ba
\Var{Y}
&= \E{\Var{Y \mid \Lambda}} + \Var{\E{Y \mid \Lambda}}
&& \text{(law of total variance)} \\
&= \E{\Lambda} + \Var{\Lambda}
&& \text{(Poisson mean and variance)} \\
&= \mu + \frac{\mu^2}{\rho}
&& \text{(moments of } \Lambda \text{)}
\ea
$$
:::
